mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's shots FOR is below its own all-prior mean AND its shots_on_target FOR rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) is simultaneously below competition baseline; measure Team A goals FOR in those joint-condition matches versus all other matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goals FOR is further suppressed when both shot volume and on-target accuracy are jointly below their respective baselines, beyond what either condition alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume deficit relative to opponents (shots FOR vs shots AGAINST) co-occurs with a low shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR), and together these two dimensions jointly predict whether Team A's goal output falls below competition baseline — the joint suppression of both volume and accuracy is structurally different from either dimension alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint two-observable conditioning (shots volume AND shots-on-target rate simultaneously), which cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band. Neither 'shots vs opponent-allowed shots' nor 'shots_on_target vs opponent-allowed shots_on_target' alone captures the interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's possession FOR (RECENT_5) is below its ALL_PRIOR mean AND Team B's shots AGAINST (RECENT_5) is above its ALL_PRIOR mean simultaneously; measure Team B goals AGAINST in those joint-condition matches versus baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B goals conceded rises when both possession deficit and elevated shots-against co-occur in recent form, more than when only one of these conditions holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent possession collapse (RECENT_5 possession FOR well below ALL_PRIOR mean) co-occurs with a simultaneous spike in shots AGAINST (RECENT_5 shots AGAINST above ALL_PRIOR), and the joint state of low possession + high shots conceded predicts elevated goals conceded beyond what either observable's trend alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires joint conditioning on two distinct observables (possession AND shots AGAINST) both in a specific directional state simultaneously — not reducible to a single observable with one band or a simple recent-vs-long-run comparison of one metric.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute Team A's home-to-away ratio of corner kicks FOR and Team B's home-to-away ratio of corner kicks FOR; condition on the cross-team asymmetry (Team A ratio substantially exceeds Team B ratio) and measure the resulting corner kick differential FOR Team A (home) vs Team B (away).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The corner kick differential favoring Team A is amplified beyond what a simple overall-mean comparison would predict, because Team A's corner production is venue-sensitive while Team B's is not — the asymmetry in venue-sensitivity compounds the home advantage.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks FOR exhibit a strong home/away asymmetry (home mean notably above away mean), while Team B's corner kicks FOR show near-zero home/away asymmetry. The asymmetric venue-sensitivity of corner production across the two teams — measured as the cross-team difference in venue-split corner ratios — predicts the corner kick differential in this fixture beyond what each team's overall corner mean would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single observable split by venue for one team. It requires comparing the venue-sensitivity ratio of one observable across two different teams simultaneously — a cross-team asymmetric two-dimensional structure that the engine's single-team venue split does not capture.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute Team A's ratio of goals AGAINST SECOND_HALF to goals AGAINST FIRST_HALF, and Team B's ratio of goals FOR SECOND_HALF to goals FOR FIRST_HALF; condition on both ratios exceeding 1.0 (i.e., both teams show second-half skew in the same direction) and measure total second-half goals in such matches versus first-half goals.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goals are elevated relative to first-half goals when both Team A's defensive vulnerability and Team B's attacking output are jointly skewed toward the second half, more than when only one team shows this skew.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal concession rate (goals AGAINST SECOND_HALF) is disproportionately elevated relative to its first-half concession rate (goals AGAINST FIRST_HALF), while Team B's second-half goal scoring rate (goals FOR SECOND_HALF) is also disproportionately elevated relative to its first-half rate (goals FOR FIRST_HALF). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry — Team A concedes more in the second half AND Team B scores more in the second half — creates a compounding second-half goals environment that is not captured by full-match averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF) applied jointly across two distinct team-perspective combinations (Team A AGAINST and Team B FOR), which is not reducible to a single observable's half split for one team or a full-match comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's fouls FOR (RECENT_5) is below its ALL_PRIOR mean AND Team B's fouls FOR (RECENT_5) is above its ALL_PRIOR mean simultaneously; within those matches, measure cards_2h FOR for each team and compare to competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's foul rate is declining while Team B's is rising, the second-half card distribution becomes asymmetric — Team B's cards_2h FOR rises relative to Team A's, diverging from the symmetric competition baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half cards environment is jointly shaped by Team A's elevated cards_2h FOR (above competition baseline) and Team B's cards_2h FOR (also above competition baseline), while both teams' fouls FOR show divergent recent trends (Team A fouls FOR declining in RECENT_5, Team B fouls FOR rising in RECENT_5). The combination of high second-half card rates with divergent foul-trend trajectories — one team fouling less recently, the other more — creates a non-symmetric disciplinary pressure in the second half that cannot be captured by either team's card or foul rate alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls trend AND cards_2h) across two teams with opposite directional trends — an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable structure that is not reducible to any single-observable or single-team band comparison.
